DRONE. The genre that is a refusal: rate 0.25, so one loop of the phrase
takes four bars, `tie` so consecutive same-pitch notes fuse into one long
one, a pedal bass that never leaves the tonic, and a reverb you could lose
a coat in. The line is there — thinned to half its notes — precisely so
that it is not a pad-only genre: something has to move or there is nothing
to listen TO, and the ramp (clamped, reversing) is what moves it.

named "New York 1964" — La Monte Young's Theatre of Eternal Music:
strings holding tones over a pedal that never moves.

LINEAGE: NO LONGER A ROOT (2026-08-29). This comment used to end
"none of which the catalog holds", and two of the three have been
held for a while: `organum` landed 2026-08-21 and this row went on
asking for it, which is what a stale `wants` looks like. Both are
paid now. Organum's sustained fifths are the claim Young made
himself (he named Perotin), and `dhrupad` is the Hindustani half —
with one caveat kept rather than tidied away: he began studying
under Pran Nath in 1970, six years after this row's label, so the
tanpura reached the Theatre of Eternal Music through records and
through Riley before it reached it through a teacher. Gagaku is
still owed.
"gagaku" PAID 2026-08-29 (Nara 752): Young named the shō's held
cluster among his sources out loud, and the weight comes off
both older claims evenly — the drone's three ancestries are now
all in the table, which no other row this old can say.

THE MODE THIS RECORD CANNOT SOUND (2026-09-02, the catalogue round,
shift 2; test/precompose.test.js G14b).
La Monte Young, New York 1964 — the row's own anchor, and a drone has no
mode: the whole refusal this row is built on is a pedal that never leaves
the tonic (`harmony: "modal"`, no kit, a bass that does not move). Nothing
in the record can state a sixth, so nothing in it can be dorian rather than
natural minor. The field now names the default alphabet it was always
playing — MEASURED, dorian -> aeolian moved not one rendered note.

the drone IS the pad; it goes first
label: New York 1964
